name: Abiel Foster
bio: a Delegate and a Representative from New Hampshire; born in Andover, Mass., August 8, 1735; graduated from Harvard College in 1756; studied theology; ordained and installed as pastor in Canterbury, N.H., in 1761 and served until 1779; deputy to the provincial congress at Exeter in 1775; Delegate to the Confederation Congress, 1783-1785; judge of the court of common pleas of Rockingham County, 1784-1788; elected as a Pro-Administration candidate to the First Congress by special election to fill the vacancy created when United States Representative-elect Benjamin West did not take his seat in the First Congress (June 22, 1789-March 3, 1791); member of the New Hampshire state senate, 1791-1794, and served as its president in 1793; elected as a Federalist to the Fourth and to the three succeeding Congresses (March 4, 1795-March 3, 1803); died in Canterbury, N.H., February 6, 1806; interment in Center Cemetery.
